label: Biodiversity
blurb: How much wetland the basin holds, and how rich it is in threatened and freshwater-dependent species.

method: Wetland area is the sum of GLWD v2 per-class area for classes 8–32 over the basin; wetland share divides it by the basin's area. Threatened species richness is the area-weighted mean of the IUCN Red List 2025 count of Vulnerable, Endangered and Critically Endangered species (amphibians, birds, mammals, reptiles, freshwater fish), on IUCN's ~10 km grid (H3 res 5). Amphibian species richness is the same for all amphibians: a freshwater-dependent group with complete global assessment, used in place of freshwater fish, whose IUCN coverage is still uneven between regions. A basin with no amphibian range scores 0. Wetland area is a total, so larger basins tend to rank higher on it; wetland share is the size-free counterpart. Basins are HydroBASINS v1c polygons as H3 res-6 cells (~36 km²): level-6 basins are filled by cell centre and coarser levels are unions of level-6 basins by Pfafstetter code. Wetland is GLWD v2 classes 8–32 (lacustrine, riverine, palustrine, ephemeral, peatland and coastal wetlands); open water and rice paddies are left out. Scores are mid-rank percentiles (0–100) among the basins at the chosen level, with direction applied so higher is better for the pillar; tied values share the midpoint of their rank range. The pillar score is the plain mean of the variable percentiles. All of this is provisional: which variables belong to which pillar, and how they are weighted, has not been decided.
